**Session ID:** `01KJR8JA0CQXS951PDBEBRA3CW`

> kspec session start --json
> ```
>

## Instructions

Run the task-work skill in loop mode:

```
/kspec:task-work loop
```

Loop mode means: no confirmations, auto-resolve decisions, automation-eligible tasks only.

**Normal flow:** Work on a task, create a PR, then stop responding. Ralph continues automatically —
it checks for remaining eligible tasks at the start of each iteration and exits the loop itself when none remain.

**Do NOT call `end-loop` after completing a task.** Simply stop responding.
`end-loop` is a rare escape hatch for when work is stalling across multiple iterations with no progress — not a normal exit path.

Implement Agent Dispatch Engine
────────────────────────────────────────
ULID:      01KJP277R7TP3HWHAMNEV2ZSB3
Slugs:     implement-agent-dispatch-engine
Type:      task
Status:    needs_work
Priority:  3
Automation: eligible
Spec ref:  @agent-dispatch-engine
Plan ref:  @plan-reactive-agent-runtime
Depends:
  @implement-agent-invocation-lifecycle → Implement Agent Invocation Lifecycle [completed]
Created:   2026-03-02T01:22:21.575Z
Started:   2026-03-02T19:08:06.052Z

─── Spec Context ───
Agent Dispatch Engine
Type: feature
Implementation: in_progress
Description:
  Core dispatch runtime that runs inside the daemon. Watches for task
  state changes via both file watcher events and direct API event
  emission from CLI commands. Matches state changes against agent
  dispatch rules, queues invocations, manages concurrency, and handles
  deduplication of events from dual sources. Serializes shadow branch
  mutations when multiple agents run concurrently.
Acceptance Criteria:
  [ac-1]
    Given: A task transitions to a state matching an agent's dispatch rule

    When: The state change is detected via file watcher or API event

    Then: The matching agent is queued for dispatch with the triggering
task reference and event metadata

  [ac-2]
    Given: Multiple agent definitions match the same state change

    When: Dispatch rules overlap

    Then: Each matching agent is queued independently, creating separate
sessions

  [ac-3]
    Given: An agent's max_concurrent limit is reached

    When: A new dispatch trigger fires for that agent

    Then: The invocation is queued FIFO and dispatched when a slot opens

  [ac-4]
    Given: The dispatch engine is running

    When: A CLI command mutates task state (e.g. kspec task submit)

    Then: The CLI posts a state change event to the daemon and the
engine processes it

  [ac-5]
    Given: The dispatch engine is running

    When: The file watcher detects a change in project.tasks.yaml

    Then: The engine diffs previous vs current task states and emits
state change events for any transitions found

  [ac-6]
    Given: A dispatch rule includes filters (automation status, tags)

    When: A state change matches the event type

    Then: The task is checked against all filters and the agent is only
queued if every filter matches

  [ac-7]
    Given: The same state transition is detected by both the file watcher
and a CLI API event

    When: Both events arrive within a short window

    Then: The dispatch engine deduplicates them using a (task_id,
from_state, to_state) tuple with a time window, dispatching
only once

  [ac-8]
    Given: The dispatch engine starts (daemon startup or explicit start)

    When: Tasks already exist in states matching dispatch rules

    Then: The engine evaluates all current task states against dispatch
rules and queues any matching agents (bootstrap/catch-up)

  [ac-9]
    Given: The dispatch engine encounters a transient error during spawn

    When: The error is an adapter timeout or process crash

    Then: The invocation is retried up to the agent's configured retry
count with exponential backoff

  [ac-10]
    Given: An agent definition's adapter reference cannot be resolved

    When: The dispatch engine attempts to spawn the agent

    Then: An error is logged with the unresolvable adapter ID, the
invocation is skipped, and a note is added to the task

  [ac-11]
    Given: The dispatch engine is stopped (daemon shutdown or explicit stop)

    When: Active agent invocations exist

    Then: Running agents receive graceful cancel signals and all sessions
are closed before the engine reports shutdown complete

  [ac-12]
    Given: Multiple agents are running concurrently (max_concurrent > 1)

    When: Both agents attempt shadow branch mutations (e.g. kspec task note)

    Then: The dispatch engine serializes shadow branch commit operations
to prevent worktree corruption from concurrent git commits


─── Notes ───
[2026-03-02T01:22:21.575Z] @claude:
Implementation notes:

New module at src/agent-runtime/dispatch.ts. In-memory queue with
configurable concurrency. Event deduplication via a Map of recent
(task_id, from_state, to_state) tuples with TTL (e.g. 2 seconds).
Bootstrap on start: load all tasks, evaluate dispatch rules, queue
matches. Shadow branch serialization: wrap kspec CLI mutations in
a queue/lock when concurrent agents are running. Task state diffing
stores previous parsed states in memory, compares on file change.

[2026-03-02T04:39:11.298Z] @claude:
Automation: eligible. Complex but well-specified with 12 ACs. Implementation notes cover queue design, dedup strategy, bootstrap behavior.
[2026-03-02T17:12:54.687Z] @claude:
Implemented DispatchEngine in src/agent-runtime/dispatch.ts. Key design decisions:

- In-memory queue with FIFO dispatch per agent, respecting max_concurrent limit
- Event deduplication via (task_id, from_state, to_state) tuple with configurable TTL (default 2s)
- Bootstrap on start: loads all tasks, evaluates dispatch rules, queues matches
- File watcher integration via FileChangeCallback in ProjectContextManager (avoids tight coupling)
- Shadow branch serialization via simple in-house Mutex (no external dep)
- specDir is configurable to support both shadow (.kspec/) and traditional mode
- Daemon routes at /api/agent/dispatch/start|stop|status and /api/agent/event (AC-4)
- 18 behavioral tests covering all 12 ACs
[2026-03-02T17:37:46.898Z] Jacob Chapel:
[FIX_CYCLE: 1] Review findings: PR #634 review findings: MUST-FIX AC gaps in dispatch engine (retry queue can stall without wake-up, unresolved adapter path does not add required task note, stop() does not send graceful cancel signals, filter matching is bypassed when task data is missing). Additional SHOULD-FIX items on prompt double-expansion and input validation posted inline. Not merged.
[2026-03-02T18:23:01.764Z] @claude:
Fix cycle 1 complete. Addressed all MUST-FIX review items from PR #634:
- AC-6: filter returns false (not true) when task data unavailable to prevent spurious dispatch
- AC-9: added setTimeout wake-up timer after retry backoff so retries don't stall
- AC-10: added kspec CLI call to add task note when adapter unresolvable
- AC-11: added AbortController per invocation; stop() aborts all active agents; added InvocationAbortedError in invocation.ts
Also addressed SHOULD-FIX items: status validation in daemon route, prompt double-expansion fix.
Added 3 new tests (AC-10 task note, AC-11 abort signal, AC-9 wake-up timer).
Branch: feat/implement-agent-dispatch-engine (PR #634).
[2026-03-02T18:36:45.728Z] Jacob Chapel:
[FIX_CYCLE: 2] Review findings: MUST-FIX: PR #634 does not fully satisfy @agent-dispatch-engine ac-10 on daemon start path. packages/daemon/src/routes/agent-dispatch.ts creates DispatchEngine without kspecCliPath, so unresolvable adapter path skips required task note. Also check-unresolved-comments CI gate is failing with unresolved review threads.
[2026-03-02T19:02:57.688Z] @claude:
Fix cycle 1 complete. All 4 MUST-FIX items addressed:
1. AC-6 filter bypass: returns false when task data unavailable (already fixed in prior commit, confirmed)
2. AC-10 task note: spawnSync kspec task note on unresolvable adapter (already fixed, confirmed)
3. AC-11 cancel signals: AbortController.abort() called on all controllers in stop() (already fixed, confirmed)
4. AC-9 retry stall: setTimeout wake-up scheduled after re-enqueue (already fixed, confirmed)

Confirmed all 23 dispatch engine tests pass.
[2026-03-02T21:39:58.279Z] Jacob Chapel:
[FIX_CYCLE: 3] Addressed latest PR #634 review feedback. MUST-FIX (shutdown race): dispatch now guards queue draining when engine is not running (early return in _drainQueues and post-invocation drain guarded after stop). Added AC-11 regression test ensuring queued work is not spawned if drain runs after stop.
[2026-03-02T22:10:03.735Z] @claude:
[FIX_CYCLE: 4] Review findings: MUST-FIX (AC-11): Daemon shutdown does not stop active dispatch engines. The engines map in packages/daemon/src/routes/agent-dispatch.ts is never iterated on SIGTERM/SIGINT, so active invocations do not receive graceful cancel signals. AC-11 specifies 'daemon shutdown or explicit stop' — the explicit-stop path is correct but daemon shutdown is missing. Need to add stopAllEngines() export and call it from server.ts shutdown handler. Posted as inline comment on PR #634 (review 3878949264).

  [ac-2] (from @trait-error-guidance)

> ```

## Instructions

Run the task-work skill in loop mode:

```
/kspec:task-work loop
```

Loop mode means: no confirmations, auto-resolve decisions, automation-eligible tasks only.

**Normal flow:** Work on a task, create a PR, then stop responding. Ralph continues automatically —
it checks for remaining eligible tasks at the start of each iteration and exits the loop itself when none remain.

**Do NOT call `end-loop` after completing a task.** Simply stop responding.
`end-loop` is a rare escape hatch for when work is stalling across multiple iterations with no progress — not a normal exit path.

Daemon Agent Dispatch Integration
Type: feature
Description:
  Agent dispatch API routes in the daemon, enhanced file watcher with
  task state diffing for change detection, CLI event emission endpoint,
  and WebSocket broadcasts for agent invocation status.
Acceptance Criteria:
  [ac-1]
    Given: The daemon is running with dispatch enabled

    When: The file watcher detects a change in project.tasks.yaml

    Then: The watcher parses the new task states, diffs against the
previously cached states, and emits state change events to
the dispatch engine for each detected transition

  [ac-2]
    Given: A CLI command changes task state (e.g. kspec task start)

    When: The daemon is running

    Then: The CLI posts a JSON event to POST /api/agent/events containing
task_id, previous_status, new_status, and timestamp

  [ac-3]
    Given: The daemon receives a state change event matching dispatch rules

    When: The dispatch engine processes it

    Then: The agent is dispatched and a status event is broadcast on the
agents WebSocket topic

  [ac-4]
    Given: A WebSocket client subscribes to agent status updates

    When: An agent invocation starts, completes, or fails

    Then: A broadcast event is sent containing session_id, agent_id,
task_id, status, and timestamp

  [ac-5]
    Given: GET /api/agent/status is called

    When: The dispatch engine is running

    Then: Returns JSON with active invocations array, queue depth number,
dispatch_enabled boolean, and agent_definitions array

  [ac-6]
    Given: POST /api/agent/dispatch is called with action start or stop

    When: The request is from localhost

    Then: The dispatch engine starts or stops and returns JSON with the
new dispatch_enabled state

  [ac-7]
    Given: The daemon is not running

    When: A CLI command changes task state

    Then: The event emission POST fails silently with no error to the
user — dispatch requires a running daemon

Fix batch exec copying sessions/blobs to temp dir
────────────────────────────────────────
ULID:      01KJQKVZ1J0SBDG9B3A3RAJBZ6
Type:      task
Status:    pending
Priority:  1
Automation: eligible
Spec ref:  @batch-write-buffer
Tags:      bug, batch, performance
Created:   2026-03-02T15:50:01.010Z

─── Spec Context ───
Atomic isolation via write buffer
Type: requirement
Description:
  Atomic batch isolation is implemented via an in-memory write buffer (overlay), not a full directory copy to /tmp.
  
  The overlay intercepts file writes during batch execution, buffering them in memory. Reads check the buffer first (returning the pending write if present), then fall through to the real .kspec/ directory. On success, all buffered writes are flushed to disk atomically. On failure, the buffer is discarded — real .kspec/ is never touched.
  
  This replaces the current fs.cp(realSpecDir, tempDir) approach in batch-exec.ts, which copies the entire .kspec/ directory including sessions/blobs/ (potentially GBs of data) for every batch run.
Acceptance Criteria:
  [ac-1]
    Given: atomic batch mode is active
    When: a command writes a file to .kspec/
    Then: the write is stored in the in-memory buffer, not written to disk
  [ac-2]
    Given: command A writes a file and command B reads the same file in the same batch
    When: command B reads the file
    Then: command B sees command A's buffered write (read-after-write consistency)
  [ac-3]
    Given: all batch commands succeed
    When: batch commits
    Then: only the buffered files (those actually written) are flushed to disk — files not touched by the batch are unchanged
  [ac-4]
    Given: any batch command fails in atomic mode
    When: batch rolls back

--- Spec Context ---
Implementing: Daemon Agent Dispatch Integration

Agent dispatch API routes in the daemon, enhanced file watcher with
task state diffing for change detection, CLI event emission endpoint,
and WebSocket broadcasts for agent invocation status.


Acceptance Criteria (7):
  [ac-1]
    Given: The daemon is running with dispatch enabled

    When: The file watcher detects a change in project.tasks.yaml

    Then: The watcher parses the new task states, diffs against the
previously cached states, and emits state change events to
the dispatch engine for each detected transition

  [ac-2]
    Given: A CLI command changes task state (e.g. kspec task start)

    When: The daemon is running

    Then: The CLI posts a JSON event to POST /api/agent/events containing
task_id, previous_status, new_status, and timestamp

  [ac-3]
    Given: The daemon receives a state change event matching dispatch rules

    When: The dispatch engine processes it

    Then: The agent is dispatched and a status event is broadcast on the
agents WebSocket topic

  [ac-4]
    Given: A WebSocket client subscribes to agent status updates

    When: An agent invocation starts, completes, or fails

    Then: A broadcast event is sent containing session_id, agent_id,
task_id, status, and timestamp

  [ac-5]
    Given: GET /api/agent/status is called

    When: The dispatch engine is running

    Then: Returns JSON with active invocations array, queue depth number,
dispatch_enabled boolean, and agent_definitions array

  [ac-6]
    Given: POST /api/agent/dispatch is called with action start or stop

    When: The request is from localhost

    Then: The dispatch engine starts or stops and returns JSON with the
new dispatch_enabled state

  [ac-7]
    Given: The daemon is not running

    When: A CLI command changes task state

    Then: The event emission POST fails silently with no error to the
user — dispatch requires a running daemon


Remember: Add test coverage for each AC and mark tests with // AC: @spec-ref ac-N

On failure, the buffer is discarded — real .kspec/ is never touched.

    When: a command writes a file to .kspec/
    Then: the write is stored in the in-memory buffer, not written to disk

    When: command B reads the file
    Then: command B sees command A's buffered write (read-after-write consistency)
  [ac-3]
    Given: all batch commands succeed
    When: batch commits
    Then: only the buffered files (those actually written) are flushed to disk — files not touched by the batch are unchanged
  [ac-4]
    Given: any batch command fails in atomic mode
    When: batch rolls back
    Then: the buffer is discarded with no disk writes — .kspec/ state is identical to before the batch
  [ac-5]
    Given: a batch runs against a .kspec/ directory containing large sessions/blobs/ data
    When: batch executes in atomic mode
    Then: .kspec/sessions/ is never copied to the temp location — only files actually written by batch commands exist in the buffer
  [ac-6]
    Given: a batch is executing and has buffered writes not yet flushed
    When: another kspec process reads .kspec/ from disk
    Then: the reading process sees the original pre-batch state (buffer is process-local and not visible outside the batch process)
  [ac-7]
    Given: all batch commands succeed but writing the buffer to disk fails partway through the flush
    When: flush encounters a write error
    Then: the error is reported and .kspec/ is left in a consistent pre-batch state — no partial writes are silently committed

**Session ID:** `01KJR8JA0CQXS951PDBEBRA3CW`
**Iteration:** 4 of 30
**Mode:** Automated (no human in the loop)

> ```
> kspec session start --json
> ```
>
> Summary: `{}`

## Instructions

Run the task-work skill in loop mode:

```
/kspec:task-work loop
```

Loop mode means: no confirmations, auto-resolve decisions, automation-eligible tasks only.

**Normal flow:** Work on a task, create a PR, then stop responding. Ralph continues automatically —
it checks for remaining eligible tasks at the start of each iteration and exits the loop itself when none remain.

**Do NOT call `end-loop` after completing a task.** Simply stop responding.
`end-loop` is a rare escape hatch for when work is stalling across multiple iterations with no progress — not a normal exit path.

import json
lines = open('/home/chapel/Projects/kynetic-spec/.kspec/sessions/01KJPDHWGZQSSMPV34A1D7Q10X/events.jsonl').readlines()

for line in lines:
    try:
        ev = json.loads(line)
        data = ev.get('data', {})
        update = data.get('update', {})
        if update.get('sessionUpdate') != 'tool_call':
            continue
        meta = update.get('_meta', {})
        tool = meta.get('claudeCode', {}).get('toolName', '')
        if tool != 'Bash':
            continue
        raw = update.get('rawInput', {})
        print(f'seq={ev.get(\"seq\")}, hasRaw={bool(raw)}, rawKeys={list(raw.keys())}')
    except:
        pass
" | head -20

    When: a command writes a file to .kspec/

    When: command B reads the file
    Then: command B sees command A's buffered write (read-after-write consistency)
  [ac-3]
    Given: all batch commands succeed
    When: batch commits
    Then: only the buffered files (those actually written) are flushed to disk — files not touched by the batch are unchanged
  [ac-4]
    Given: any batch command fails in atomic mode
    When: batch rolls back
    Then: the buffer is discarded with no disk writes — .kspec/ state is identical to before the batch
  [ac-5]
    Given: a batch runs against a .kspec/ directory containing large sessions/blobs/ data
    When: batch executes in atomic mode
    Then: .kspec/sessions/ is never copied to the temp location — only files actually written by batch commands exist in the buffer
  [ac-6]
    Given: a batch is executing and has buffered writes not yet flushed
    When: another kspec process reads .kspec/ from disk
    Then: the reading process sees the original pre-batch state (buffer is process-local and not visible outside the batch process)

--- Spec Context ---
Implementing: Atomic isolation via write buffer

Atomic batch isolation is implemented via an in-memory write buffer (overlay), not a full directory copy to /tmp.

The overlay intercepts file writes during batch execution, buffering them in memory. Reads check the buffer first (returning the pending write if present), then fall through to the real .kspec/ directory. On success, all buffered writes are flushed to disk atomically. On failure, the buffer is discarded — real .kspec/ is never touched.

This replaces the current fs.cp(realSpecDir, tempDir) approach in batch-exec.ts, which copies the entire .kspec/ directory including sessions/blobs/ (potentially GBs of data) for every batch run.

Acceptance Criteria (7):
  [ac-1]
    Given: atomic batch mode is active
    When: a command writes a file to .kspec/
    Then: the write is stored in the in-memory buffer, not written to disk
  [ac-2]
    Given: command A writes a file and command B reads the same file in the same batch
    When: command B reads the file
    Then: command B sees command A's buffered write (read-after-write consistency)
  [ac-3]
    Given: all batch commands succeed
    When: batch commits
    Then: only the buffered files (those actually written) are flushed to disk — files not touched by the batch are unchanged
  [ac-4]
    Given: any batch command fails in atomic mode
    When: batch rolls back
    Then: the buffer is discarded with no disk writes — .kspec/ state is identical to before the batch
  [ac-5]
    Given: a batch runs against a .kspec/ directory containing large sessions/blobs/ data
    When: batch executes in atomic mode
    Then: .kspec/sessions/ is never copied to the temp location — only files actually written by batch commands exist in the buffer
  [ac-6]
    Given: a batch is executing and has buffered writes not yet flushed
    When: another kspec process reads .kspec/ from disk
    Then: the reading process sees the original pre-batch state (buffer is process-local and not visible outside the batch process)
  [ac-7]
    Given: all batch commands succeed but writing the buffer to disk fails partway through the flush
    When: flush encounters a write error
    Then: the error is reported and .kspec/ is left in a consistent pre-batch state — no partial writes are silently committed

Remember: Add test coverage for each AC and mark tests with // AC: @spec-ref ac-N
